Author: Prakash Chandra Gupta
Bench: Prakash Chandra Gupta

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 Cra No. 5936 of 2024
 (Yogesh Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh )
 Dated : 12-12-2024
 Shri Harshvardhan Pathak, learned counsel for the appe
 Shri Hemant Sharma, learned Govt.Advocate for the resp
Heard on I.A.No.11074/2024, which is first application under Section 389 of Cr.P.C./430 of Bnss
for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellant - Yogesh .

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The learned Trial Court has convicted the appellant for offences punishable under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC and sentenced him to undergo ten years' RI with fine of Rs.2,000/-, under Section 452 of IPC and sentenced him to undergo five years' RI with fine of Rs.1,000/- and under Section 506(2) of IPC and sentenced him to undergo five years' RI with fine of Rs.1,000/-, with default stipulation vide judgement of conviction and order of sentence dated 3.5.2024 passed by the 1st Addl.Sessions Judge, Sanawad, Distt. Mandleshwar (West Nimar) in Sessions Trial No.01/2022.

entities.text: 1st Addl.Sessions Judge, Sanawad, Distt. Mandleshwar (West Nimar)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. As per prosecution case, the appellant is friend of prosecutrix's husband and used to visit her house.
At around three years before lodging the FIR, when husband of the prosecutrix was not present at his house, appellant went to the house of prosecutrix and committed rape upon her.

He threatened her that if she will narrate the incident to someone, he will kill her and her children,
therefore, she did not narrate the incident to her husband.
Thereafter, applicant repeated the aforesaid act several times.

The matter was 2 CRA-5936-2024 reported on 27.11.2021.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant has not committed any offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.

It is submitted that it can be easily inferred from para 12 to 15 of cross- examination of the prosecutrix that she was consenting party for sexual intercourse, but the trial Court without considering the aforesaid statement of the prosecutrix wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant.
It is further submitted that appellant has completed incarceration around 52 days during trial of the case and after conviction he completed incarceration around six months.
Final hearing of this appeal will take sufficient long time therefore, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended and he be released on bail.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection.

sentences.text:
6. Considering the short term of sentence coupled with the fact that final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case,
I.A.No.11074/2024 is allowed and jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended till the final disposal of this appeal.

7. It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if already not deposited, appellant - Yogesh shall be released on bail, on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of Trial Court, for his appearance before the Registry of this Court firstly on 5.2.2025 and on such other dates, as may be 3 CRA-5936-2024 fixed by the Registry in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
List for final hearing in due course.
